name: Eastern Cattle-Egret
rangeDescription: Southern and eastern asia to australia and new zealand
description: Small, compact white heron with relatively short yellow bill. More often seen in dry habitats than other egrets, but also frequent in rice paddies and shallow wetlands.

name: Yellow-rumped Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern asia; winters in southeastern asia and greater sundas
description: Gaudy male striking, with yolk-yellow underparts and rump and black upperparts set off by white supercilium and wing patch. Female less brightly colored but still distinctive, with brown upperparts, a smaller yellow rump and white wing patch, and whitish underparts with faint scaling on the breast.

name: Orinoco Softtail
rangeDescription: Upper río orinoco in eastern colombia (eastern vichada and eastern guainía) and western venezuela (northwestern amazonas)
description: Distinctive rounded-tailed rufous-brown bird of riverine habitats. Narrow buffy eyebrow and buffy streaks on cheeks and breast.

name: Red-bellied Grackle
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia
description: Unmistakable Colombian endemic: large, long-tailed, and all-black with a bright red belly and piercing yellow eye. Sexes similar.

name: Prairie Falcon
rangeDescription: Arid north america (british columbia to northern mexico)
description: Large, brown-and-white falcon of dry, open areas in western North America. Pale brown above and white below, with dark streaks and prominent mustache.

name: El Oro Parakeet
rangeDescription: Andean foothills of southwestern ecuador (el oro and azuay)
description: Rare and endangered parakeet endemic to foothill cloud forest in southwestern Ecuador. It is mostly green with red on forehead, shoulder, and undertail.

name: Olive Spinetail
rangeDescription: Eastern paraguay to southeastern brazil (são paulo) and northeastern argentina
description: Restless long-tailed species with an olive-brown back, whitish chin, and buffy underparts. Note the whitish eyebrow, rusty wing patch, and rusty tail.

name: Madagascar Wagtail
rangeDescription: Open country and streams throughout madagascar
description: Elegant, long-tailed bird with a gray back, pale underparts, and a black chest band. White wing patch and outer tail are conspicuous in flight.

name: Brown-backed Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (southern bahia to rio de janeiro and são paulo)
description: Small parrot with a short, squared tail that has red outer tail feathers with a black band across the tips. Mostly green with a brown patch on the back and pale gray flanks.

name: Blue-capped Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (sierra de miahuatlán of oaxaca)
description: Endemic and distinctive, medium-sized hummingbird found in the foothills of the Sierra Madre del Sur in Oaxaca. Favors humid evergreen forests and shade-coffee plantations.

name: Blue Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Sierra leone to gabon, democratic republic of the congo and southwestern uganda; bioko island
description: A beautiful, entirely blue thrush-like bird that can be surprisingly hard to make out in the dark subcanopy of tropical forests as it forages high above the ground. When seen well, it is unmistakable, with its entirely blue body, red eyes, dark face, and black bill.

name: Smooth-billed Ani
rangeDescription: West indies, southeastern mexico (quintana roo) and costa rica southward to western ecuador and northern argentina, also galapagos (introduced); formerly southeastern usa (florida, where now rare)
description: Anis are bizarre, coal-black cuckoos with long floppy tails and unique, curiously tall, flattened bills. Smooth-billed occurs in a variety of open and semi-open habitats in tropical lowlands and foothills, typically staying low in shrubs and grasses.

name: Camiguin Hanging-Parrot
rangeDescription: Camiguin (philippines)
description: A very small parrot of upland forest on Camiguin island. Overall green in color with a bluish face, an orange bill and legs, and a red crown and rump.

name: Pesquet's Parrot
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed mountains of new guinea
description: A large, primitive parrot of lower-montane, foothill and nearby lowland primary forest. Unparrotlike, long, pointy head.

name: Blue-banded Toucanet
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern peru (huánuco) to southern bolivia (santa cruz, chuquisaca)
description: Small green toucan of humid montane forest. Blue chest band is distinctive but can be difficult to see; notice also the bluish coloration in its face and bill and the yellowish bill tip.

name: Little Bunting
rangeDescription: Taiga of northern eurasia; winters to india, southeastern asia, and philippines
description: Small bunting with an attractive contrasting head pattern: black crown with red-brown central stripe and pale eyering. Rufous cheeks bordered by narrow black lines framing the eyes.

name: Omani Owl
rangeDescription: Distribution poorly known; documented from northeastern united arab emirates, northern oman, northeastern iran, and southwestern pakistan
description: Pale, medium-sized owl of dry rocky country with cliffs and canyons. Dark brown above and pale with narrow dark streaks below.

name: Rufous-headed Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Western ecuador and far northwestern peru
description: Large chickenlike bird with a long tail. No similar species in limited range; much smaller than Crested Guan and warmer brown than Sickle-winged Guan.

name: Variable Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela, the guianas, and northern amazonian brazil
description: Slender, long-tailed, chickenlike bird that is often seen in small groups. Grayish-brown overall with a warmer chestnut head.

name: Chestnut Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northern peru (amazonas south of the río marañón, southward to huánuco, and north of the río huallaga)
description: Plain antpitta restricted to cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern Peru. Mostly chestnut-brown; very similar to Graves’s Antpitta, but lacks a distinct eyering and has a different voice.
